answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independently sampled audits show fabricated results or collusion. Reputation is tied to the locked stake and accrues only through verified tasks, so minting a thousand identities does not create a thousand trustworthy agents. An attacker must fund each identity, keep capital tied up, and risk losing it; splitting stake among accounts does not evade the total cost. A sonnet, a jade shipment, or a tide forecast earns standing only when its result survives review.
